note: 30 fictional dreams written for this project. Nobody dreamed these. The labels are hand-assigned ground truth: water means a body of water or water itself is part of the imagery (ocean, sea, lake, river, pool), pursuit means the dreamer is being chased, followed or hunted. Several dreams are deliberate hard negatives (running for a train, chasing a kite, snow, a sink).

dreams.text: I was back in my grandmother's house, but the staircase kept going up past the attic. Every landing had a door, and behind each door was the same kitchen with the kettle boiling. I climbed for what felt like hours. At the top there was a window, and through it I could see the ocean far below, completely still. I felt calm, like I had been expecting it.

A man in a grey coat was chasing me through a supermarket at night. The aisles kept rearranging and my legs moved like I was wading through glue. I knocked over a tower of tins to slow him down. When I finally reached the exit the doors would not open, and I woke up with my heart pounding.

My teeth started crumbling while I was giving a presentation at my old school. I kept spitting pieces into my hand and trying to carry on talking. My maths teacher sat in the front row writing notes and nobody else seemed to notice. I was so embarrassed I wanted the floor to swallow me.

I was swimming in warm water under a huge yellow moon. The water was so clear I could see a city on the bottom, with street lamps still lit. A whale passed underneath me, slow and enormous, and I was not afraid at all. I floated on my back and watched the stars. It was the most peaceful I have felt in months.

I was late for a train and running along the platform with a suitcase that kept getting heavier. The station clock had no hands. A conductor waved at me from the last carriage but the train pulled away anyway. I stood there holding a ticket for a place I had never heard of, feeling stupid and a bit lost.

Something was following me down a long hotel corridor. I never saw it, but every time I stopped, its footsteps stopped half a second later. I tried every door and they were all locked. The carpet got thicker until it was like walking through deep sand, and the footsteps kept getting closer behind me. I was too scared to turn around.

I found a small brass key in the garden of my childhood home. It opened a door in the trunk of the apple tree, and inside was a library with a spiral staircase. My mother was there, younger than I have ever seen her, shelving books. She smiled and said I was right on time. I felt safe and very small.

The ocean came up the street like a slow grey wall. I was on the roof of our house with my brother and our dog, watching cars float past. Nobody panicked. We started fishing off the chimney and my brother caught a bicycle. It all seemed completely normal and a little bit funny.

I was flying over a forest at dusk, only a few metres above the trees. I could steer by leaning. Birds flew alongside me and one of them had my father's voice, telling me to keep my arms straight. It was wonderful. Then I got too high, the air went thin, and I started to fall.

Wolves were hunting me through deep snow. I could hear them breathing behind me and I kept falling over. I reached a cabin and slammed the door, but the windows had no glass. I hid under a table and held my breath, terrified, listening to them circle outside.

I was sitting an exam in a huge hall and the paper was written in a language I could not read. Everyone else was writing fast. My pen turned into a feather and then into a small fish that slipped out of my fingers. The invigilator looked exactly like my dentist. I felt sick with panic.

I was in a rowing boat on a lake with my grandfather, who died years ago. The water was black and perfectly flat. He pointed at the mountains and told me the names of things I could not see. I wanted to stay, but the boat kept drifting back to the shore. I woke up missing him.

There was a baby in my arms that I had forgotten I had. I was at an airport and could not find the right gate, and the baby kept shrinking until it fit in my coat pocket. I was so worried about losing it. A stranger offered to hold it for me and I could not decide whether to trust her.

A black car was tailing me while I rode my bicycle home. Every corner I took, it took. I cut through a park and across a bridge, pedalling as hard as I could, and it was still there behind me with its headlights off. I could not see a driver. My chest was tight with dread.

I was standing in front of a mirror in a bathroom that was not mine. My reflection was a few seconds behind me. When I raised my hand it waited, then raised the other one. Then it turned and walked out of the frame, and I was left looking at an empty room. It was strange more than frightening.

I walked into the sea in my work clothes. The waves were warm and loud. My colleagues were all there already, standing up to their necks, holding a meeting. My boss handed me a wet folder and I remember thinking it was important not to drop it. Nobody thought any of this was odd.

My old dog was alive again and we were walking through a field of very tall sunflowers. She kept running ahead and coming back. The sun was low and everything was gold. I knew it was a dream and I tried to walk slowly so it would last. I woke up happy and then sad.

Security guards were after me in a museum because I had touched a painting. I ducked behind statues and ran up a marble staircase that turned into an escalator going the wrong way. I could hear their radios getting nearer. I climbed into a sarcophagus to hide and tried not to breathe.

The house had a room I had never noticed, behind the bookcase. It was full of clocks, all showing different times, and a piano covered in dust. I felt guilty, like I had been neglecting it. Through its window there was a garden in full sun, though it was night everywhere else.

I was driving a car from the back seat and could barely reach the wheel. The road went down a mountain in tight curves and the brakes did nothing. My sister was asleep in the front. I steered with a piece of string and somehow we kept making the bends. I was anxious the whole way down.

I was at the bottom of the ocean and could breathe. There was a door in the sand, standing upright with no wall around it. Light came through the keyhole. I knew that if I opened it all the water would drain away, so I just sat next to it with a crab. It was quiet and I was content.

A swarm of bees pursued me across a football pitch. I could not outrun them. I pulled my jacket over my head and crawled into a goal net, and they covered it like a curtain. The buzzing sounded like people whispering my name. I was frightened but I could not make a sound.

I was in an elevator that went sideways. The buttons were labelled with the names of people I went to school with. I pressed one and the doors opened onto my childhood bedroom, with my bed still unmade. The elevator would not wait for me. I remember a strong feeling of homesickness.

A river ran through the middle of the office. People stepped over it without looking. I knelt down and the water was full of tiny silver keys moving like fish. I filled my pockets with them and they melted. I was confused about why nobody else wanted any.

I was on a stage and did not know the play. The audience was all children in animal masks. Someone in the wings kept whispering my lines but in the wrong order. A curtain came down made of heavy red velvet and I felt relieved, almost grateful.

Footsteps came up the stairs behind me in my own apartment block. I climbed faster, two steps at a time, and whoever it was sped up too. I got to my front door and the key bent like rubber in the lock. I could feel them right at my back. I woke up afraid to move.

I was a child again at the swimming pool, standing on the highest diving board. The water looked like glass. My mother was waving from the side. I jumped and never landed, just kept falling through blue. It was not frightening. It felt like being let off something.

A snake was coiled in the kitchen sink. It was not threatening, just there. I made tea around it. When I looked again it had become a garden hose and my grandmother was telling me off for leaving it out. I felt like a child, annoyed and fond of her at once.

I was climbing a mountain made of books. Some of them were mine. Near the top there was a small fire and a stranger keeping it going with pages. He offered me a seat. The moon was close enough to touch and it was cold as a coin. I felt a kind of awe.

I chased a red kite across a hillside for what felt like miles. The string was always just out of reach. The grass was long and silver in the wind. A windmill turned slowly at the far end, and I was laughing the whole way. I woke up in a good mood.
